sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Financial behavior among youngsters has undergone considerable transformation in the digital era. Easy access to online banking, digital wallets, instant credit systems, and e-commerce platforms has made financial transactions more convenient than ever before. However, financial experts argue that such convenience has also encouraged impulsive spending and weakened the traditional culture of savings among young people. Many adolescents and young professionals increasingly associate financial success with visible consumption rather than disciplined wealth management. Social media platforms further intensify this trend by promoting luxury lifestyles and instant gratification. Economists warn that inadequate financial literacy at an early age can lead to long-term debt dependency and poor investment decisions. Consequently, educational institutions and financial organizations have begun introducing programs on budgeting, saving, taxation, and responsible borrowing. Advocates of financial education believe that cultivating saving habits during youth not only improves individual economic security but also contributes to broader economic stability within society.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The Indian Premier League (IPL) has transcended the boundaries of a mere sporting tournament to become a colossal socio-economic phenomenon. While purists lament the “Disneyfication” of the gentleman’s game—citing the erosion of technical finesse in favor of brute force and theatrics—the league’s economic footprint is undeniable. It has democratized cricket remuneration, pulling obscure domestic talents from hinterlands into the limelight of financial security. However, this commercial juggernaut raises pertinent questions regarding the commodification of national sentiment. The franchise model, heavily borrowed from American sports, risks diluting regional loyalties in favor of corporate identities. Furthermore, the relentless schedule contributes to player burnout, often rendering national duty secondary to contractual obligations. The challenge lies in balancing this commercial vitality with the sanctity of the sport, ensuring that the spectacle does not cannibalize the very skill set it intends to celebrate.

questions.q: A ladder leaning against a vertical wall makes an angle θ with the ground such that sin θ = 0.8. If the top of the ladder reaches 24 m up the wall, find the horizontal distance from the wall to the foot of the ladder.
questions.why: Ladder = 24 ÷ 0.8 = 30 m; base = √(30² − 24²) = 18 m (3-4-5 triangle). GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Concert ticket prices for VIP, Executive and Economy are in the ratio 5 : 3 : 2. In a sale, VIP gets 20% off and Executive 10% off; Economy has no discount. If an Executive ticket costs ₹2,700 after discount, what is the combined cost of one ticket of each category in the sale?
questions.why: Executive full price 3000, so 1 part = 1000. 4000 + 2700 + 2000 = 8700. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The average age of 15 students increased by 2 years when two students aged 14 and 18 were replaced by two new students. If one new student is 12 years older than the other, find the age of the younger new student.
questions.why: Total rises by 30, so new pair = 32 + 30 = 62. x + x + 12 = 62 gives 25. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The Banker's Discount on a bill is 6/5 times the True Discount. If the rate of interest is numerically 5 times the number of years for which the bill is due, find the rate.
questions.why: BD/TD = 1 + RT/100 = 6/5, so RT = 20. With R = 5T: T = 2, R = 10%. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: In a non-leap year, a month contains exactly five Sundays, five Mondays and five Tuesdays. Which month could it be?
questions.why: Three days repeating five times needs a 31-day month; only August has 31 days. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: 3 senior and 5 junior technicians finish a project in 8 days for a total wage of ₹2,400. 2 seniors and 10 juniors finish it in 6 days. What will a team of 4 seniors and 5 juniors earn per day on an identical project?
questions.why: 24S + 40J = 12S + 60J, so 3S = 5J. First team is worth 10J and earns 2400 ÷ 8 = 300/day, so J = 30, S = 50. 4 × 50 + 5 × 30 = 350. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Statement: "The delay in the project is due to a shortage of materials." Which judgment is most reasonable?
opts: The shortage of materials is the sole cause of the delay
There could be other factors contributing to the delay
The delay is not due to the shortage of materials
The shortage of materials has nothing to do with the delay
questions.why: Accept the stated cause without making it the only one. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: In an artificial language, migenlasan means cupboard, lasanpoen means boardwalk and cuopdansa means pullman. Which word could mean "walkway"?
questions.why: lasan = board, so poen = walk; the word must start with poen and not use migen (cup). GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: What is the next term? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ?

questions.q: Tree is to leaf as flower is to:

questions.q: Acute diseases (§72) are described as:
opts: rapid morbid processes of the abnormally deranged vital force that tend to end in recovery or death within a moderate time
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Chronic diseases, by contrast, keep developing.

questions.q: Hahnemann held that too large a dose of even the right remedy (§275–276):
opts: may do harm, by producing a strong aggravation or new medicinal symptoms
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hence the minimum dose.

questions.q: Who proved Lachesis in 1828 and is called the father of American homoeopathy?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hering also gave the law of direction of cure.

questions.q: Eruptions with thick, hard crusts under which yellow pus collects, intense itching, and neuralgia after herpes zoster suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Mezereum: crusts with pus beneath, post-herpetic neuralgia.

questions.q: Shortness of breath with dry, barking, croupy cough like a saw through a pine board, worse before midnight, calls for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Spongia: sawing cough.

questions.q: Threatened abortion at about the third month with bright-red, partly clotted bleeding and pain from the sacrum to the pubis calls for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sabina: sacrum-to-pubis pain.

questions.q: Haemorrhages of bright red blood, burning pains, desire for cold drinks and fear in a tall, slender, sympathetic person suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Phosphorus: bright red bleeding, craves cold water.

questions.q: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, a homoeopathic medicine that is not of standard quality as per the HPI is called:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. 'Spurious' means imitation or substituted drugs.

questions.q: The sugar of milk used in homoeopathy is chemically:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. A disaccharide of glucose and galactose.

questions.q: Repertories based on the pathological and clinical approach, such as Boericke's, are useful mainly when:
opts: the case is full of mental symptoms
characteristic symptoms are few and the diagnosis is clear
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Clinical rubrics help when characteristic symptoms are lacking.

questions.q: The 'Mind' chapter rubric 'Consolation agg.' would lead to remedies such as:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Pulsatilla and Phosphorus are ameliorated by consolation.

questions.q: The deltoid muscle is supplied by the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Injured in shoulder dislocation and surgical-neck fractures.

questions.q: Most of the water filtered by the kidneys is reabsorbed in the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. About two-thirds of filtered water.

questions.q: Raised serum alkaline phosphatase with mildly raised ALT and AST and conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia suggests:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. ALP is the marker of bile-duct obstruction; transaminases are very high in hepatitis.

questions.q: Chikungunya is characterised by fever with:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. The name means 'that which bends up'.

questions.q: A 'resting tremor' that improves with movement, with rigidity and slow movement, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Pill-rolling tremor.

questions.q: Constipation in infants with hard stools that recede after being partly expelled ('bashful stool') suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Silicea's shy stool.

questions.q: Severe pain at the close of urination, with the patient able to pass urine freely only when standing, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Sarsaparilla: pain at the end of micturition.

questions.q: The commonest cause of secondary amenorrhoea in women of reproductive age is:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Always exclude pregnancy first.

questions.q: Kangaroo mother care is recommended for:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Skin-to-skin contact for warmth and breastfeeding.

questions.q: The commonest site of a varicose ulcer is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. From venous hypertension.

questions.q: Neck pain and stiffness radiating to the arms with numbness, in an elderly patient with osteophytes on X-ray, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Degenerative disease of the cervical spine with root compression.

questions.q: A 'sentinel surveillance' system is used mainly to:
opts: detect trends in diseases through selected reporting sites
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Used for HIV and others.

questions.q: Snake venom that is mainly neurotoxic, causing ptosis and paralysis, is typical of the:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Vipers are mainly haemotoxic.

questions.q: Under the law, a doctor's professional records should generally be preserved for at least:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. As per the medical ethics regulations.
